flawed_step: The exchange-argument step: 'if an optimal solution O differs from the greedy solution G at the first item where they disagree, swap part of O's lower-ratio items for the greedy item without losing value.' Because items can't be split in 0/1 knapsack, taking the higher-ratio item can use up space that lower-ratio items would otherwise fill completely. So the swap may lower the total value, and the step can't be justified. (The argument only works for fractional knapsack.)
counterexample: W=10; items A(w=6,v=7, ratio 7/6), B(w=5,v=5, ratio 1), C(w=5,v=5, ratio 1). Greedy takes A first, leaving 4 capacity, so B and C don't fit: value 7. Taking {B,C} weighs 10 and is worth 10 > 7.
assessment_summary: I tried to prove the statement with the standard greedy exchange argument. That argument needs items to be divisible, which 0/1 knapsack doesn't allow, so the step fails. A small instance confirms it: greedy by ratio gets 7, while the optimum is 10. The statement is false.
